scope: Replay the old spatial preprocessing on all 29 retained historical continuum-fit candidate channels, then compare spatial scale diagnostics. No channel selection from current intensities or gravity scoring.
reference_preprocessing: scripts/run_gravity_cube_pilot.py: prepare, recorded additional circular Gaussian smoothing, scipy default truncate=4, zero extension, float32 intermediate planes, 8x8 arithmetic block mean, original full-annulus parity-zero per-channel offset subtraction.

operation.spectral_order_contract: Require native FELO-HEL with negative CDELT3 and the cache audit VOPT-F2W. Only reverse stored channel indexes; no velocity or spectral response fit is performed.
operation.offset_border_test: xx>6, yy>6, xx<nx-7, yy<ny-7, matching the original prepare routine

independent_benchmarks: FFT finite convolution versus direct summation with zero extension
Gaussian impulse flux and centroid conservation away from boundaries
Block averaging preserves integrated pixel sum after multiplying by block area
Recorded per-channel offset replay reproduces each cached selected plane

spatial_diagnostic.center: Native FITS reference pixel, evaluated at each 8x8 coarse-cell center
spatial_diagnostic.method: Per-channel Gaussian-scaled MAD, medians and tails in both regions, without fitting a covariance law to force agreement. No statistical pass threshold is selected for these descriptive ratios.

nonclaims: Replay success validates this preprocessing implementation, not the physical accuracy of the old beam model
The extra circular smoothing does not make the full native elliptical beam exactly circular
The resulting intensity units remain Jy per native beam, not Jy per 48-arcsec beam
Historical continuum-fit candidates can retain faint line emission or instrumental structure
Median scale agreement does not establish a full covariance, selection function or galaxy likelihood
